data.title: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:19 (`_parsed`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_parsed` short-circuits on `_MARK in text`, i.e. it skips `RG.parse` entirely whenever the literal substring `ddflow:begin` does not occur, and returns `[]` — which is exactly the "no regions, nothing to report" answer rather than the "markers unreadable" answer. So a hand-edit that removes the begin marker line (`<!-- ddflow:begin doc/page <hash> -->`) while leaving the matching `<!-- ddflow:end doc/page -->` in place — a common botched merge-conflict resolution — turns into silence: `problem()` returns `""` and `edited()` returns `[]`, so the pre-commit check and the doctor note both read the file as a clean whole-file document and let it through. An orphaned end marker is the textbook "unbalanced" marker case the module docstring promises is reported by `problem`, and the body hash can no longer be checked at all once the begin marker is gone. `mask()` has the same hop (it returns `_parsed()`, so a `RegionError` path is never reached here either), leaving the leftover template lines in the text docscheck prose-checks. The guard should only elide the no-marker-at-all case (which `RG.parse` already answers with `[]`); as written it also elides the malformed case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:19 (`_parsed`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_parsed` now returns `[]` for the *entire document* as soon as one adopt-stamped block is found anywhere in it: `any(m in text for m in _MARKS) and not _STAMPED.search(text)`. A file that legitimately contains both an adopt-stamped block and a real generated region therefore stops being parsed at all. Concretely, given

```
<!-- ddflow:begin rules/work-queue ddflow=0.2.0 fmt=1 sha=f60922c1c1f6 -->
x
<!-- ddflow:end rules/work-queue -->
<!-- ddflow:begin doc/page deadbeef -->
hand-edited body
<!-- ddflow:end doc/page -->
```

`_STAMPED.search` matches the first line, so `problem(text)` returns `""` and `edited(...)` returns `[]` — the hand-edited `doc/page` region is exactly the thing the pre-commit enforcement is supposed to refuse, and it is silently accepted; the hash check is bypassed for that file. The same short-circuit breaks the other direction for `mask`: an unstamped-but-real region's generated body is left in the text, so `docscheck` prose-checks generated region content it was meant to exclude, producing false findings, while the stamped block is (correctly) skipped. The previous code (`_MARK in text`) did parse such a mixed document; this change regresses it by keying the decision off the presence of any stamped block rather than off the region under inspection. The `_STAMPED` check needs to be per-region (or the stamped lines excised/neutralized before `RG.parse`), not a whole-text veto. Note also that a stamped-looking line inside a fenced code example in an otherwise real region-bearing doc triggers the same whole-file silence.

titles: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:19 (`_parsed`) — the `_STAMPED` guard is all-or-nothing over the whole text

chunk_findings.detail:
Presence of any adopt-stamped marker anywhere in the file turns the whole file into "no regions" for this module. `_parsed` returns `[]` whenever `_STAMPED.search(text)` matches, so for a document that carries both a pinned block and a region — exactly the coexistence the guard was written for, since adopt writes pinned `ddflow:begin NAME ddflow=V fmt=N sha=H` blocks into documents that also get refreshed regions, e.g.

```
<!-- ddflow:begin security ddflow=v1 fmt=2 sha=... -->
...
<!-- ddflow:end security -->
<!-- ddflow:begin docs/api sha=... -->
hand-edited body
<!-- ddflow:end docs/api -->
```

`edited(text)` returns `[]` and `problem(text)` returns `""`, so the new pre-commit check and the doctor both read the hand-edited region as clean (only the separately-implemented whole-file header check in `enforce.py` can still fire); this contradicts the module's own contract that "could not tell" is never read as clean, because here the region text *was* readable and a body mismatch *was* knowable. The same guard makes `mask()` a no-op on that file, so docscheck's prose checks still run over generated region bodies — the very thing this change says docscheck should stop doing. A narrower treatment (drop/ignore only the stamped markers, or parse the two grammars side by side) would keep region coverage while still not reading an adopt end marker as unbalanced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/region_check.py:20 (the `_STAMPED` guard in `_parsed`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`notes.write_text("# Notes

my words

" + RG.render_region("roadmap", "body", "stale region
"))` replaces a literal region whose header carried a deliberately non-matching digest (`body-sha256=000000000000`) with a region produced by the same renderer that refresh/ops use to emit valid, self-consistent regions. The written body is `stale region
` and the header digest is now the correct `sha256` of exactly that body, so the condition this test exists to provoke — region body ≠ region header hash — is no longer present. Under the enforcement mechanism described in the intent (refuse a staged region whose body does not match its hash, implemented via the new `region_check` helpers `_parsed`/`edited`), that mismatch is the only signal that would make `_commit(proj, "NOTES.md", ".ddflow")` fail; a matching digest means the region parses as clean and is not hand-edited, so the commit the test expects to be refused is allowed (or, at best, the test now only exercises the staleness path and the hand-edited/hash-mismatch path it was written for is silently dropped). The fix is to keep the rendered region but tamper with it — e.g. render, then overwrite the `body-sha256=` value (or change the body after rendering) — rather than using the renderer's own output verbatim. Nothing in the other files listed in the manifest changes this: `render_region` is the producer of valid regions, not of mismatched ones, so no other part of the change supplies the missing corruption.
